subject: orientdb as a new sql backend??

messages.author: a11d4d45419f6981
messages.subject: orientdb as a new sql backend??
parts:
Hi, I was reading https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dplyr/vignettes/new-sql-backend.html and trying to understand whether orientdb could be added as a new sql backend. Orientdb is a mix of a document and graph database, but uses a SQL language for querying. That being said, what starts as SQL later gets extended "to support more complex graphing concepts, such as Trees and Graphs"  http://orientdb.com/docs/2.1/Tutorial-SQL.html

to summarize, my question at this point is simply: how can I evaluate whether an orientdb backend for dbplyr would be possible?

ricardo

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: orientdb as a new sql backend??
parts:
Hi Ricardo,

I think the best way to start is to think about how you'd translate
basic dplyr verbs (e.g. filter(), arrange(), mutate()) in to
operations in OrientDB.

Hadley
